168.s: A Binghamton friend wrote scores featuring the bass; Stewart performed with the Binghamton and Indianapolis symphonies.
168.q: Well, I would say that I didn't exactly encounter any classical bassists, but how it happened was that -- well, let's start off like this. I had a friend of mine right here in Binghamton write a few scores for me to play with symphonic orchestras and they were written so that I could be the feature…

168.t: Playing jazz cadenzas with string quartets and a woodwind quintet
168.s: With the Lincoln String Quartet and a woodwind quintet at the Robeson Center music conference he played classical works with jazz cadenzas between movements, 1970-72.
168.q: I've done quite a bit of work with the Lincoln String Quartet of Southern Illinois and the Camarado (PHONETIC) Woodwind Quintet of Western Illinois University and we have done quite a bit of work, especially for the -- sponsored by the National Council on the Arts.

168.t: Binghamton Symphony, Jack Martin's score, and the yearly projects
168.s: He played with the Binghamton Symphony, premiered Jack Martin's A Symphonic Dream for Slam, and the wives sort out the baroque, harpsichord and jazz-group projects.
168.q: The second year, he worked with a harpsicordist doing the same baroque music. I mean, also baroque, not the same music, but also baroque.

168.t: Future plans: Berklee, Boston Pops, and new orchestral scores
168.s: Stewart plans Berklee and Boston Pops dates, San Francisco has called, and young composers are writing five new scores for orchestras of 50 to 80.
168.q: Jack Martin, the one. But a young student who is terribly talented named Bobby Frankivello (PHONETIC), he did one symphonic score for Slam when he was 18 that was quite successful and now he's 19.

107.s: The commission yielded seven pieces he still performs, including Sugar Hill Slalom.
107.ch: Cecilia, Elvin Jones and jazz education
107.q: That Lake Placid Suite was a significant commission from the Jazzmobile. It didn’t receive much prominence, because in the setting of Lake Placid, most of the people who were there, their musical orientation was not jazz. Kenny Rogers, the Kenny Rogers of pop music fame, and Tanya Tucker and all…

107.s: He hopes for total theater, a jazz mass and a jazz opera, and mentions Carnegie Hall Jazz Band commissions.
107.ch: Current bands, plans and the second Basie tenure
107.q: I don’t have any commissions working at the moment, so my plans are to develop these three groups with the emphasis on the two larger groups, the big band, the Loud Minority, and Swing Plus, to expand their repertoires, and to make total musical statements through those groups, and to try to make…

187.t: Pritchard's symphony orchestra and Professor Blanchard
187.s: The Grand Lodge convention job in Shreveport, and where pianist Blanchard now teaches.
187.q: Pritchard he tried to arrange a symphony orchestra, yes sir. He was doing nicely with it. The Grand Lodge gave a session, I had the convention out in Shreveport. We went out there and played at that big auditorium, it sounded fine. And that night we played two nights out there for them. First night…

721.s: Malone arranged orchestral pop hits for a symphony with rhythm section and tells of a fundraiser at North Texas.
721.q: And my recent project is that I arranged a pop symphony act for myself. It’s a symphony orchestra with a rhythm section. And the concept is orchestral pop hits of the twentieth century. Stuff like “MacArthur Park,” “Unforgettable,” “Georgia On My Mind,” “Kashmir,” “Bet You By Golly Wow,” you know,…

617.t: Quiet Pride, inspired by Elizabeth Catlett
617.s: His commissioned suite inspired by Elizabeth Catlett's sculptures and plans to bring jazz, art and studies departments together.
617.q: Well I do want to talk about, you weren’t here, because I had my, it’s actually one of my most ambitious things, the Quiet Pride, which is the music that I was commissioned to write, inspired by Elizabeth Catlett’s sculptures. And that’s going to come out officially hopefully in September of this…

722.s: Recent string project for John Nugent and yearly writing for Jim Doser's high school studio orchestra.
722.ch: Listening, jazz history and the future
722.q: I do. I just did a big project last summer for John Nugent, strings from the RPO and harp and jazz rhythm section, all in jazz standards. So John played that during the jazz festival and it was my first conducting with the baton experience in Eastman Theater and two thousand people. It’s supposed…
